# 0006: The release SBOM is generated by catalog-tools from a checked inventory

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-11-25
- Deciders: catalog maintainers
- Affects: the repository's tooling and CI (`sbom` and `release_assets` jobs,
  `ci/sbom-sources.yml`); no variable, tag, profile, platform or schema
  changes in this record
- Issues: catalog#21; catalog#22 (locked CI toolchain); hypervoid/admiral#136

## Context

The first SBOM (`scripts/build_collection_sbom.py`) listed the files of the
artifact only. A lab could not tell from a release what the collection pulls
in: its collection dependencies, the tools that built it, or the repositories,
downloads and installer scripts the roles use on a host. A Python extension
(!169) was closed unshipped under the no-new-Python rule
(hypervoid/admiral#136), and #21 was briefly routed to launch-sequence's
supply-chain stage; the collection-specific knowledge (which URL in a role is
an APT repository and which an API endpoint) lives here, so the generator does
too.

Existing SBOM generators (syft, cdxgen, cyclonedx-py) read package manifests.
They can list `ci/requirements.txt`, but none understands Ansible role
defaults and tasks, so the runtime half would still need code.

## Decision

- `catalog-tools sbom` (the Rust crate of decision 0005) generates CycloneDX 1.6
  and replaces the Python script.
- Runtime sources are a curated inventory, `ci/sbom-sources.yml`, held to the
  roles by the generator: every URL in role defaults, tasks, vars and handlers
  and every package-manager module must be declared, and every declaration
  must still match. Versions and checksums come from the role defaults the
  inventory points at.
- Schema validation uses `check-jsonschema` from the hash-checked CI lock
  against the vendored CycloneDX schema, offline.
- `catalog-tools sbom --check` is the completeness gate on the published file.

## Safety impact

Nothing changes on a research machine: this record touches CI, the tool crate
and docs only. The SBOM, the vendored schemas and `ci/sbom-sources.yml` are
excluded from the collection artifact, and no role, default, variable or tag
changes. What could go wrong is a red pipeline when a role gains an undeclared
source; the fix is a declaration in `ci/sbom-sources.yml`, not a role change.

## Alternatives considered

- An off-the-shelf generator (Syft, cdxgen): they read lockfiles and package
  databases, so they would list the CI toolchain but not the vendor
  repositories, direct downloads and installer scripts that the roles name in
  YAML, which is what #21 asks for.
- Extending `scripts/build_collection_sbom.py`: ruled out by the no-new-Python
  feature code rule (hypervoid/admiral#136).
- SPDX 2.3: equally valid; CycloneDX has first-class `scope` and component
  properties for telling source files, runtime sources and CI tools apart, and
  a JSON schema that validates offline.

## Consequences

- Adding a download, repository or installer to a role fails CI until it is
  declared, so the SBOM cannot fall behind the roles.
- Package names installed from a registry are not listed one by one; their
  source is. A host's update SBOM records the installed packages.
- Scripts in `files/` and `templates/` are outside the scan and declared by
  hand (docs/sbom.md, Limits).
